questions.question: What does the name Avicenna represent in relation to Avicenna's full Arabic name?
options: A Latinized version of the Arabic patronym ibn SÄ«nÄ
A title meaning 'father of early modern medicine'
A court title granted by the Samanid rulers
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Avicenna is a Latinized version of the Arabic patronym ibn SÄ«nÄ, indicating descent from a line of men going back to one named Sina.
Incorrect. 'Father of early modern medicine' is a description of Avicenna's role, not the meaning of his name.
Incorrect. The article does not present Avicenna as a Persian poetic pseudonym.
Incorrect. The article does not describe Avicenna as a court title granted by the Samanid rulers.

questions.question: Which two works are identified as Avicenna's most famous?
options: The Book of Healing and The Canon of Medicine
Danish-nama-yi Ala'i and a medical treatise about the pulse
answer_explanations: Correct. The article identifies The Book of Healing and The Canon of Medicine as Avicenna's most famous works.
Incorrect. The Almagest and Euclid's Elements are works Avicenna studied, not his own most famous works.
Incorrect. The Isagoge and the Categories are works Avicenna studied with al-Natili, not his own most famous works.
Incorrect. Danish-nama-yi Ala'i and a medical treatise about the pulse are Persian works Avicenna dedicated to Ala al-Dawla, not his most famous works.

questions.question: In which languages did Avicenna write most of his philosophical and scientific works?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Avicenna wrote most of his philosophical and scientific works in Arabic.
Incorrect. The article says he wrote several key works in Persian, but most were in Arabic.
Incorrect. Greek is not mentioned as a language in which Avicenna wrote his works.
Incorrect. Latin is not mentioned as a language in which Avicenna wrote his works.

questions.question: What methodological approach does Avicenna combine in his works, especially in The Canon of Medicine?
options: Empirical observation, philosophical reasoning, and logical analysis
Divine revelation, scriptural exegesis, and mystical intuition
Astrological calculation, alchemical experimentation, and poetic composition
Legal reasoning, theological debate, and historical narration
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Avicenna combines empirical observation, philosophical reasoning, and logical analysis, especially in The Canon of Medicine.
Incorrect. Divine revelation, scriptural exegesis, and mystical intuition are not described as Avicenna's methodological approach.
Incorrect. Astrological calculation, alchemical experimentation, and poetic composition are not described as his methodological approach.
Incorrect. Legal reasoning, theological debate, and historical narration are not described as his methodological approach.

questions.question: Which dynasty provided a thriving atmosphere for scholarly development in eastern Persia, Greater Khorasan, and Central Asia?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Samanid Empire provided a thriving atmosphere for scholarly and cultural development in those regions.
Incorrect. The Buyid dynasty is described as ruling in western Persia and Iraq, not eastern Persia, Greater Khorasan, and Central Asia.
Incorrect. The Ghaznavids are mentioned only in connection with the brief occupation of Isfahan.
Incorrect. The Kakuyids are mentioned as the dynasty of Ala al-Dawla, not as the dynasty providing the atmosphere in eastern Persia and Central Asia.

questions.question: By what age had Avicenna memorized the entire Quran?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that by the age of 10, Avicenna had memorized the entire Quran.
Incorrect. The article specifies age 10, not 12.
Incorrect. The article specifies age 10, not 15.
Incorrect. The article specifies age 10, not 18.

questions.question: Who did Avicenna's father invite to their house to educate Ibn Sina?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Avicenna's father invited the physician and philosopher al-Natili to educate Ibn Sina.
Incorrect. Abu Nasr Mansur is mentioned as a mathematician at the court of Gurganj, not as the tutor invited to Avicenna's house.
Incorrect. Qumri is mentioned as a physician Avicenna likely had as a teacher, but not as the one invited by his father.
Incorrect. Al-Tha'alibi is mentioned as a philologist at the court of Gurganj, not as the tutor invited by Avicenna's father.

questions.question: In what year did Avicenna move to Gorgan due to necessity?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Avicenna moved to Gorgan in 1012 due to necessity.
Incorrect. 999 is the year the Samanid Empire fell, not when Avicenna moved to Gorgan.
Incorrect. c. 1014 is when Avicenna went to Ray, not Gorgan.
Incorrect. 1021 is the year Shams al-Dawla died, not when Avicenna moved to Gorgan.

questions.question: What position did Shams al-Dawla force Avicenna to become after his campaign against Abu Shawk?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that after Shams al-Dawla's campaign against Abu Shawk, he forced Avicenna to become his vizier.
Incorrect. Avicenna had served as a physician earlier, but Shams al-Dawla forced him to become vizier.
Incorrect. Avicenna reportedly served as business manager for Sayyida Shirin, but this was not the position forced by Shams al-Dawla.
Incorrect. Avicenna may have succeeded his father as governor of Harmaytan, but this was not the position forced by Shams al-Dawla.

questions.question: During which period did Avicenna complete The Book of Healing while writing 50 pages a day?
options: While in hiding with Abu Ghalib al-Attar
While serving as physician to Nuh II
While serving Ala al-Dawla in Isfahan
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that during his stay at Attar's home, Avicenna completed The Book of Healing, writing 50 pages a day.
Incorrect. Avicenna served as physician to Nuh II at age 17, before completing The Book of Healing.
Incorrect. Avicenna was vizier to Shams al-Dawla before going into hiding with Attar.
Incorrect. Avicenna served Ala al-Dawla in Isfahan after being released from prison, not while writing 50 pages a day at Attar's home.
